title: Noun affixes
summary: Affixes that make new nouns: -an (aklátan), ka-…-an (kaligayáhan), mag- (mag-asawa), mang- (manggagamot), pag-, sang-, tag- (tag-ulán), taga- (tagaturò), tala-…-an (talátinígan), plus ways to make nouns plural
goals: Use -an to name a place, a season or an instrument (aklátan, anihán, inúman)
Use a doubled root + -an for a miniature or an imitator (baháy-baháyan, harí-harían)
Use ka-…-an for an idea or a group (kaligayáhan, kabukirán)
Use mag- and mang- for relationships and jobs (mag-asawa, manggagamot)
Use pag-, sang-, tag-, taga- and tala-…-an to make new nouns
Make nouns plural in four different ways

blocks.t: In Lesson 31 you made nouns by putting **ang**, **ng** or **sa** in front of a verb or an adjective. In this lesson you meet **affixes** (pieces added to the front or end of a root word) that turn a verb or an adjective into a noun, or even turn one noun into a different noun.
Each affix below has a **formula** (how the word is built) and a **meaning** (what kind of noun it makes). Learn the formula and you can recognise many new words from roots you already know.

blocks.title: How to read the formulas
items: **root** = the basic word, such as aklát (book).
**-an** at the end = a suffix; **ka-** at the front = a prefix.

blocks.t: Root + -an: a place where things are stored or placed
Root + -an: a season
Root + -an: an article or instrument

blocks.title: -an or -han?
blocks.t: The book names this suffix **-an or -han**. You can see -han in **anihán** (from áni) and **kabutíhan** (from buti).
When the root is **said twice, joined by a hyphen**, and then **-an** is added, the new noun means either a **small version** of the thing or a **copycat** who only pretends.

head: Root
New noun
rows: pretending to be like a mother
blocks.title: An imitator or copycat
Barò = damit
blocks.t: The book explains **barò** with another Tagalog word, **damit** (Lesson 7: damít = cloth; dress). So barú-barúan, *doll clothes*, are tiny clothes.
Put **ka-** in front of the root and **-an** (or **-han**) after it. The new noun is either an **idea** (a concept) or a **group**.

head: Root
New noun
rows: refers to a language or people
blocks.title: A group
Sound changes when a suffix is added
items: Roots that **end in o** (lutò, barò) or have **o in the last syllable** (inóm, pások): the **o changes to u**. lutò → **lutuán**, barò → **barú-barúan**, inóm → **inúman**, pások → **pasukán**.
Roots that **end in d** (bukid): the **d becomes r**. bukid → **kabukirán**.

blocks.title: Two groups you can see
blocks.t: Compare **bahayán** (group of houses, section 1) with **kabahayán** (place of many houses). Both come from báhay; the book gives them slightly different meanings.

sections.title: Mag- and mang-: family pairs and jobs

blocks.t: Mag- + root: a relationship
**Mag-** in front of a family word names the **pair** in that relationship. If the root starts with a **vowel**, put a **hyphen** after mag-.
Mag- + first syllable doubled + root: a job
Mang- or man- + first syllable doubled + root: a job

**Mang-** also names a **work or profession**. As with other prefixes, roots starting with **d, l, r, s and t** use the variant **man-** instead of mang- (the same pattern you saw with kasíng- and kasín- in Lesson 11).
You met these in Lesson 38. **Pag-** makes a **gerund** or **verbal noun** (the name of an action, like *walking* or *reading*). Which pattern you use depends on the affix the verb had.

head: Verb
Verbal noun
blocks.title: 1. Pag- replaces -um- (add a hyphen if the root starts with a vowel)

head: Verb
Verbal noun
blocks.title: 2. Pag- + doubled first syllable replaces mag-

sections.title: Sang- and tag-: wholes, ones and seasons

blocks.t: Sang- + ka- + root + -an: the whole of
**Sang-** changes to **san-** before roots starting with **d, l, r, s and t**, and to **sam-** before roots starting with **p** (as in Lesson 13 on numbers).
Sang- + root: one

head: Root
New noun
blocks.title: One
blocks.note: santaón shows san- before t. The book's example sambuwán uses sam- before b.

blocks.t: Tag- + root: season or time of

blocks.title: Two ways to say harvest time
blocks.t: **anihán** (áni + -han, section 1) and **tag-ani** both mean *harvest time*.

sections.title: Taga- and tala-…-an: people and lists

blocks.t: Taga- + name of a place: a native or resident of

items.tl: Ang mga taga-baryo ay marúnong magtaním.
items.en: Those from the barrio know how to plant.

blocks.t: Taga- + root: one who often does the action
**Taga-** + a root names **one who frequently acts out the root**: the person whose job or habit it is.

head: Book sentence
Taga- word
rows: Ang kartéro (postman) ay tagadalá ng sulat.
Si Julia ay tagabilí ng pagkain sa palengke.
Ang áking maybahay ang tagalutò námin.
blocks.title: The book's sentences
blocks.note: The book does not translate these four sentences.

blocks.t: Tala- + root + -an: a list
**Tala-** + root + **-an** names a **list of things connected with the root**.

blocks.title: A misprint in the book
blocks.t: The book's heading is **TALA- + -AN**, but its formula line says *(taga- + root + -an)*. Every example starts with **tala-**, so tala- is the prefix to learn here.

Remember the **plurality rule** from Lesson 4: when the subject is plural, nouns, verbs, articles, prepositions and question words become plural too. Here are four ways to show that a **noun** is plural.
1. Use plural articles
Use **siná** with proper nouns (names) and **ang mga** with common nouns.
2. Use a number, ilán or marami before the noun
3. Use a plural adjective
Plural adjectives follow the formula **ma + duplicated first syllable + root**.

items.tl: Mababaít na batà ang inyóng mga anák.
Báhay na malalakí ang nákita námin.

blocks.t: 4. Say the root word twice

items.tl: Pumaroón kamí sa mga baháy-baháy sa Lingayen.
items.en: We went from house to house in Lingayen.

items.tl: Bumilí kamí ng mga bágay-bágay para sa kusína.
items.en: We bought several things for the kitchen.

blocks.title: Not the same as baháy-baháyan
blocks.t: **baháy-baháy** (the root said twice) shows many houses: *from house to house*. **baháy-baháyan** (doubled + -an) is a **playhouse**.

blocks.title: Remember
items: -an: a place (aklátan), a season (anihán) or a thing you use (inúman).
Doubled root + -an: a miniature (baháy-baháyan) or a copycat (harí-harían).
Ka-…-an: an idea (kaligayáhan) or a group (kabukirán). o → u and d → r before a suffix.
Mag-: a pair (mag-asawa) or a job (magbibigás). Mang-/man-: a job (manggagamot, mandaragát).
Sang-: the whole of / one. Tag-: a season. Taga-: from a place, or one who does. Tala-…-an: a list.
Plural nouns: siná / ang mga, a number or ilán / marami, a plural adjective, or a doubled root.

recap: -an makes a place (aklátan), a season (anihán) or a thing you use (inúman); a doubled root + -an makes a miniature (baháy-baháyan) or a copycat (harí-harían).
Ka-…-an makes an idea (kaligayáhan) or a group (kabukirán). Before a suffix, o becomes u and a final d becomes r.
Mag- names a pair (mag-asawa) or a job (magbibigás); mang-/man- names a job (manggagamot, mandaragát).
Pag- makes verbal nouns: pag-alís, pagsusulát, pagbása.
Sang- = the whole of / one (sangkapuluán, santaón); tag- = a season (tag-ulán); taga- = from a place or one who does (tagaturò); tala-…-an = a list (talátinígan).
Plural nouns: siná / ang mga, a number or ilán / marami, a plural adjective (mababaít), or a doubled root (baháy-baháy).
